name: Urban Company Ltd
title: Urban Company Ltd - 544515 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Urban Company is a demand-led marketplace story, not a capital-cycle one: no capacity or capex signals, NTV up 42% YoY in Q4, and InstaHelp losses of ₹119 Cr drive the reported loss.

utilisation.quote: increasing utilization on the side and not decreasing utilization

triggers.label: Competitors raising money, price intensity
triggers.quote: competitors raise money. In pockets, one can see irrational

evasions.topic: AOV sensitivity and steady-state unit economics
evasions.quote: in the core, the sensitivity is low

summary.headline: Urban Company Q4 FY26 NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore, with Services ex-InstaHelp adjusted EBITDA margin at 3.3% and Q4 PAT of ₹98 crore hit by InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss.
summary.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly NTV, with Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore and FY26 NTV up 33% to ₹4,290 crore. Core Services ex-InstaHelp grew 26% YoY to ₹808 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 3.3% of NTV from 1.6% a year earlier. International (UAE and Singapore) turned profitable for FY26 at ₹6 crore, and Native narrowed its loss to ₹31 crore. InstaHelp absorbed ₹119 crore of Q4 losses, which drove reported Q4 profit to ₹98 crore; management is investing heavily in InstaHelp and held its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA targets.

financial_highlights.value: ₹131 crore (4.1% of NTV) — 3.3% of NTV for Services adjusted EBITDA as per call
financial_highlights.change: Services margin 1.6% of NTV in Q4 FY25
Entirely attributable to InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss; ex-InstaHelp adjusted profit ₹22 crore

segments.name: Core Services (ex-InstaHelp)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹808 crore, up 26% YoY; adjusted EBITDA ₹131 crore at 4.1% of NTV (3.3% of NTV in Services overall as stated). Management said the segment was loss-making as recently as FY24.

segments.name: International (UAE + Singapore)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹211 crore (+84% YoY) despite a March UAE headwind from the Middle East conflict; FY26 NTV ₹700 crore (+75%) with FY26 EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore.

segments.name: Native
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹89 crore (+67% YoY); FY26 NTV ₹345 crore (+122%) with loss narrowing to ₹31 crore (-8.9% of NTV) from ₹39 crore (-25.1%) in FY25.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of ₹119 crore covering acquisition, network subsidies and onboarding; 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone crossing 1.1 million orders. Targets EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28.

guidance_outlook: InstaHelp EBITDA break-even target retained at Q3 FY28.
Company-level EBITDA target of ₹1,000 crore by FY31 retained.
Management will not be giving quarterly call commentary on InstaHelp dynamics; detail is in the shareholder letter.
Management expects Services adjusted EBITDA as % of NTV to keep rising, aiming for 10% over a longer horizon; progress to be judged year-on-year rather than quarter-on-quarter.
No timeline given for Native break-even; management said it is fairly confident of the trajectory.
No incremental geography planned for the foreseeable future; focus remains India, UAE, Singapore and the KSA JV.
Native targets quadrupling net revenue with water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Services now covers 60-plus cities across 47 cities' hundreds of micro-markets; densification is the priority over coverage expansion.
UC Instant (30 to 60 minute service) rolled out; management says it improves partner packing efficiency and utilisation rather than reducing it.
AI used to audit 100% of proof-of-work images; 55% of partner support queries handled by AI; about 90% of code shipped with GenAI assistance.
Saudi Arabia JV showing improving margins with visibility towards profitability.
InstaHelp expansion kept calibrated; management leaning towards densifying existing micro-markets.
demand_pricing: Services NTV growth accelerated: 19% in Q2 FY26, 21% in Q3, 26% in Q4 (ex-InstaHelp).
Management said the Middle East dip was visible month-on-month but YoY growth stayed healthy and the business is nearly back to recovery.
No material disruption from the state election-related workplace displacement; handled through pre-onboarding of professionals.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp described as irrational at times but manageable; management said it will optimise for share rather than unit-economic elegance.
AOV sensitivity described as low in Core; management said AOV can move up or down and it will be managed through tactics and strategy.
Contribution per order declined in Q4 as InstaHelp marketing and subsidies rose; management said the decline was largely due to one cost metric (cost per order).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Services ex-InstaHelp growth to 25% in top 10 cities, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to densification flywheel effects: higher utilisation, lower travel and faster fulfilment via UC Instant, improving retention. Growth accelerated from 19% to 26% over three quarters; management wants to see more quarters before calling it a structural trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will AOV pressure and elevated competitive intensity hurt steady-state economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA guardrails but declined to give a steady-state unit-economics range, citing the need to flex tactics on AOV and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What timeline and drivers exist for Native break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Native's loss narrowed to -8.9% of NTV from -14.7% earlier; management is fairly confident of break-even but gave no timeline, and said it would happen despite new product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new product pipeline for Native to meet its quadrupling target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current launches are water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline set, and revenue to come from installed-base growth and retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the InstaHelp versus core structure a concern given competitor fundraising and is there a diversification plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees a winner-take-most dynamic in trust-based services, is targeting leadership in InstaHelp, and is not worried about competitor funding; InstaHelp average rating 4.7 and retention claimed as industry-leading.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand into new geographies or adjacencies?
qa_highlights.answer: No new geography planned in the foreseeable future; no experimentation in adjacencies. Focus is entirely on densifying core micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: What was the contribution-per-order decline and cause in InstaHelp Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing elevated to acquire users and build the brand, including Cricket World Cup spend; all metrics improved except contribution per order, which declined largely due to one cost line.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses (₹119 crore in Q4) and break-even target of Q3 FY28; reported profit depends on InstaHelp spend.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp and rising AOV pressure; management declined to quantify steady-state unit economics.
Middle East conflict effects on UAE business in March and the pace of recovery.
Native break-even has no timeline; new products (water purifiers, smart locks) not yet material.
Seasonal cost spikes in Q1/Q3 marketing ahead of peak quarters, which complicates quarter-on-quarter comparisons.
Whether Services adjusted EBITDA margin can rise from 3.3% toward 10% of NTV over a multi-year horizon.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Core and International execution, and defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, where management refused to give steady-state or quarterly guidance. Management repeatedly described competitive irrationality as manageable and said it is prioritising market share over short-term margins.
key_quotes: We are investing to win, and we intend to stay in it.

growth.why: Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 cr with Services ex-InstaHelp up 26% and accelerating; guidance held (InstaHelp EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28, ₹1,000 cr group EBITDA by FY31), backed by densification and margin expansion but no specific capacity or order numbers.
